mappings.applicability_reason: No administrative or operator interface is among this threat's affected components (cmp-003/004/005/006); the non-applicable condition 'no administrative interface exists' holds for this threat's scope.

The non-applicable condition 'every model output is rendered to a person and acts on nothing' holds: agents see a suggested reply and decide whether to use it, with no automated action loop (evd-001).
The non-applicable condition 'all outputs are drafts a person publishes manually' holds: the suggested reply is a draft the agent may edit or discard before use (evd-001).
The non-applicable condition 'the model produces text only and invokes nothing' holds: the reply service generates suggested-reply text with no described tool invocation (evd-002).
The non-applicable condition 'the system uses no external tool protocol' holds; no tool servers or MCP-style integrations appear in this threat's attack path.

This requirement addresses untrusted content redirecting a model's task at inference time. Thr-003's attack path concerns the integrity of the vendor-supplied base model itself (df-004), not content submitted with a request altering the model's task.
The non-applicable condition 'a human approves each publication and this is documented' is supported: agents decide whether to use each suggested reply before any external publication (evd-001).

The data flow in this threat's attack path (df-004) carries the base model from the vendor into the tuning job; it is not a flow of customer content sent out to an external model provider, which is what this requirement addresses.
Thr-003's impact concerns manipulated reply content and provenance, not markup injection at render time; no evidence in this threat's scope concerns encoding of rendered output for the agent console.
This threat does not involve end-user authentication; none of the affected components (cmp-003/004/005/006) provide end-user login functionality relevant to the compromised-base-model path.
No administrative or externally reachable privileged interface is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No multi-tenant request-scoping concern is implicated; this threat concerns model artifact integrity, not tenant-boundary enforcement.

The system holds no delegated access to an external platform in this attack path; the vendor supplies a model to the system rather than the system acting on a customer resource via delegated privileges.

The tuning job's fine-tuning run incorporates the vendor's base reply model as a third-party component (evd-002), meeting the 'builds incorporate third-party components' condition; thr-003's attack path is precisely a failure to identify or control that component before use, and authentication/encryption for its transfer are unrecorded (df-004).
No backup-administration concern is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No metered-infrastructure cost-abuse concern is implicated by this tampering/supply-chain threat.
No production/non-production environment separation concern is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No deployment-pipeline-definition change-visibility concern is described in this threat's scope; the attack path concerns the vendor-supplied base model rather than pipeline-definition tampering.
No alert-volume or alert-routing concern is implicated by this threat.

This requirement addresses confidentiality protection of sensitive data. Thr-003 is a tampering/integrity concern about model substitution rather than a confidentiality concern, and the transferred artifact (model weights, df-004) carries no stated sensitivity classification.
No retention-period concern for by-product customer data is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No per-tenant artifact separation concern is implicated; the artifact bucket holds a single tuned-model artifact per week, not per-tenant customer artifacts.
No customer-initiated data-deletion concern is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No redirect-based sign-in flow is implicated by this threat.
No externally issued identity token is consumed anywhere in this threat's attack path.
No delegated sign-in session is established in this threat's attack path.
No authorization-code exchange occurs anywhere in this threat's attack path.

This threat's affected components and attack path concern the vendor-supplied base model and artifact-serving path; the training corpus's write path (transcript exporter, training store) is not among the affected components of thr-003, so this requirement's governed-write-path concern does not bear on it.
Same scope reasoning as req-TRAIN-001: thr-003 does not implicate training-corpus content minimization, only the vendor-supplied base model and artifact pipeline.

Tuned artifacts are produced weekly and served to agents (evd-004), meeting the condition 'tuned model artifacts are produced and served.' The existing dated-bucket control (ctl-002) provides ordering by export date, but its documented limitation is that base-model identity and training-data snapshot version are not recorded per artifact, so lineage sufficient to trace a compromised base model into a specific served artifact is only partially established.
No application-logging-of-restricted-data concern is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No administrative-action-recording concern is implicated; this threat's attack path does not involve a privileged operator interface.
The non-applicable condition applies in substance: the reply model produces suggested-reply text that is never executed as code by the system (evd-002).
No model-generated code, configuration, or infrastructure definitions are merged or deployed in this threat's attack path.

This threat's attack path is the vendor-to-tuning-job model transfer and the artifact-serving path, not network reachability of an internal data store from an untrusted network; no evidence describes such reachability in this attack path.
No retrieval-augmented-generation corpus is described; the reply model is fine-tuned on the training store, not retrieval-augmented at answer time (evd-002).
No retrieval corpus with differing entitlements is implicated; the system is a fine-tuning pipeline, not a retrieval-augmented one.
No retrieval index derived from mutable sources is implicated; the system is a fine-tuning pipeline, not a retrieval-augmented one.

It is not established whether the tuning job holds a credential authenticating it to the vendor for the base-model transfer; evd-002 describes no such credential, and the transfer's authentication mechanism is unrecorded, so whether the condition 'the system holds a credential that authenticates it to an external platform' holds cannot be determined from the documentation.

The non-applicable condition 'the system accesses no customer resources on external platforms' fits this attack path: the vendor supplies a model to the system, the system does not access a customer resource held on an external platform.

Thr-003's attack path (df-004) is inbound -- the vendor's model to the tuning job -- not customer data sent out to an external provider. Whether transcript data separately reaches the vendor is an unresolved, distinct question (qst-001) that does not form part of this threat's stated attack path.
No metered-external-service-triggered-work bounding concern is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No inbound webhook or event endpoint is implicated by this threat's attack path.
No inbound event replay concern is implicated by this threat's attack path.

documentation_gaps.title: Base model provenance and integrity verification are undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: The tuning job fine-tunes the vendor's base reply model (evd-002), but the documentation does not describe how that base model's authenticity or integrity is verified before use, nor how the transfer from the vendor is authenticated or encrypted (df-004 records both as unknown).
documentation_gaps.importance: Without a stated verification step, a substituted or tampered base model would carry that compromise into every weekly tuned artifact and every suggested reply served to agents, with no documented point at which the substitution would be detected.
requested_evidence: Documentation of the authentication and encryption used for the base-model transfer from the vendor
Description of any integrity check (checksum, signature, pinned version, or vendor attestation) applied to the base model before it is used for fine-tuning

documentation_gaps.title: Tuned artifact lineage does not record base model identity or training-data snapshot
documentation_gaps.description: Tuned artifacts are named by export date in the artifact bucket (evd-004), and the existing control (ctl-002) is documented as covering only this date-based naming; it does not state that the base model's identity or the training-data snapshot version is recorded against each artifact.
documentation_gaps.importance: Without recorded base-model identity per artifact, a compromised base model's presence in a specific served artifact cannot be traced, and remediation cannot selectively identify which tuned artifacts derive from the affected base model version.
requested_evidence: Confirmation of whether the artifact bucket or a registry records the base-model version or identifier used to produce each tuned artifact
Confirmation of whether the training-data snapshot version is recorded per artifact
